title: Is it possible to generate smaller than 16x16 pixel art using AI?
author: TheOnlinePolak
selftext: I've created a puzzle game that requires extra small pixel art anywhere between 2x2 and 10x14 px art in size. Most are is 10x10 and it rarely gets smaller than 4x6 but I do have some weird shapes like 2x8. Is there a way to generate pixel art this small automatically? I have not seen a way smaller than 16x16 and making the art myself does take lots of time.

replies.author: denzelgamedev
replies.body: Give Pixel Lab a try, seemed pretty good.

comments.author: j____b____
comments.body: Just draw 2 x 2 pixels. It is a total of 4 pixels. Too much to do by hand?

replies.author: TheOnlinePolak
replies.body: I very very rarely reach the minimum. I need the art to actually be art. The end goal of the puzzle is to reveal an image. A 2x2 block of solid color is not really what I'm looking for.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: just use something like gimp and change the resolution, it would lower the number of pixels and give the best attempt and keeping it similar. Ai can't work at that scale.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
2x2 is literally one order of magnitude away from a solid block of color.  There really isn't any visual data being conveyed there.

Even 10x10 is incredibly tiny, just draw that by hand.  No diffusion model is going to be able to coherently generate a concept at such a small size, and downscaling from 1024x1024 is going to look terrible.

replies.author: TheOnlinePolak
replies.body:
People seem to be dead set on me saying 2x2, that was just a hard minimum. I recognize no art will be that small in reality. The smallest puzzle art I’ve made was 3x9 and I’m sure it would be an image people would recognize.

I did some messing around and although no AI model is perfect and probably won’t be, they are great for a rough draft even at my pixel size limitations. I’ve found Gemini shockingly does the best at making a rough draft at this size.

replies.author: SpecialistProper3542
replies.body: You can't have actual art in a 2x2 space it is literally four squares. I think you'd be better off doing some research and figuring out what you're actually talking about instead of using AI to make games..

replies.author: TheOnlinePolak
replies.body: The game is made. People play it. I make art for it. Not good art because I’m not an artist but it is art nonetheless. People are stuck on the 2x2 but I said. That’s just a hard cap. The smallest puzzle I’ve made is 3x9. I can make the art by hand. But I’ve also hired artists and their art is better. Just wanted to see if AI was an option.

replies.author: SpecialistProper3542
replies.body:
That makes no sense. Hard cap means the max. 3x9 is bigger than 2x2 pixels

3x9 is also insanely small I don't think you understand what you're saying

replies.author: TheOnlinePolak
replies.body:
Whatever, my phrasing was off. I need micro pixel art. I already have 70+ pieces of art between 3x9 and 10x14. I understand that is very small. I also know it’s possible because I’ve done it already. Check for yourself if you want. Here’s the 3x9 puzzle which is pretty simple to solve. The image although not detailed is recognizable.

[Pixolve Puzzle #41](https://www.pixolve.co/puzzle/20260610)

replies.author: SpecialistProper3542
replies.body:
Ok I did a puzzle, the image was not recognizable and if it didn't say it was a wine bottle I would have had no idea. I think trying to prompt an AI to do this would take way more time than just making it yourself. 

Just take a picture and shrink it down to that size then change the palette to a few colours if you're really stuck.

comments.author: quantum-elle
comments.body: You could try generating a grid of small icons, or generate your sprite at a higher resolution then either scale it down or trace it. Low res pixel art, especially at that size, is going to be challenging with current diffusion models.

comments.author: last1031
comments.body: not yet, not well. even 32x32 is rough if not using something super specialized and trained for it. anything smaller is not happening atm.

comments.author: Glittering-Fan-1178
comments.body: It sounds like this could be achieved procedurally through code. Try describing the variants you want to AI and ask it to write a script with Python/pillow that you can use to give inputs and produce the art for you.

comments.author: Sufficient-Pop-1643
comments.body: I really don't understand why you need AI for such small images. It seems like it would take less time and effort if you just did it yourself.
